title: Where do we place brackets to get the stated value?
description: Three expressions without brackets are given a stated value by placing brackets in the right place. Each placement is checked by working out the value.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: a bracket after a minus sign takes away a whole group together. Ask the child to work out the value after placing the bracket.

video_script.why: The child places brackets so that the value comes out as stated, using the idea that a bracket after a minus sign takes away a whole group.
video_script.substitution: The same idea works with other numbers: decide what must be taken away together, then put it in a bracket.
video_script.anchor: three expressions without brackets, each with the value it must give
video_script.payoff_line: A bracket after the minus sign takes away the whole group.

final_answer.spoken: thirty four minus the bracket nine plus twelve equals thirteen; the bracket fifty six minus fourteen, minus eight, equals thirty four; minus twenty two minus the bracket twelve plus ten, plus twenty two, equals minus twenty two

maths_rules: a bracket after a minus sign takes away its whole group; a bracket after a plus sign changes no term
video_script.design: One idea: a bracket after a minus sign takes away a whole group together. The three expressions stay in the anchor band; the working band shows each bracket and its value. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first expression is thirty four minus nine plus twelve, and it must be thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirty four minus twenty one is thirteen, and twenty one is nine plus twelve.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Put the bracket round nine plus twelve to take both away together.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We get thirty four minus the bracket nine plus twelve.

marks.m2: 42 − 8 = 34 is written and matched with the stated value

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, in the second expression, fifty six minus fourteen is forty two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Forty two minus eight is thirty four, which is already the stated value.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A bracket round fifty six minus fourteen keeps that value.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, as printed, the third expression comes to minus two.
We need minus twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Put the bracket round twelve plus ten, so the minus takes away both.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That gives minus twenty two minus twenty two plus twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each one by working out the value.
Thirty four minus twenty one is thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Forty two minus eight is thirty four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Minus twenty two minus twenty two is minus forty four, and plus twenty two makes minus twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>A bracket after the minus sign takes away the whole group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We get thirty four minus the bracket nine plus twelve, which equals thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then the bracket fifty six minus fourteen, minus eight, which equals thirty four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Then minus twenty two minus the bracket twelve plus ten, plus twenty two, which equals minus twenty two.
